newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo says higher pulp prices unlikely in Q1.
newsitem.headline: MoDo says higher pulp prices unlikely in Q1.

text.p: Swedish forestry group MoDo AB said on Thursday that it was hard to see higher pulp prices in the first quarter of 1997.

MoDo's chief analyst Soren Nordin said at a forestry seminar in Stockholm he saw North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp inventories rising to over two million tonnes in the first quarter of the year.
"NorScan inventories will increase in the next few months and they will surpass two million tonnes...Thereby it will be hard to raise prices in the short term," Nordin said.
In the second quarter and during the rest of the year, inventories will fall to just below 1.5 million tonnes, according to Nordin.
At the end of December 1996, NorScan stocks were at more than 1.9 million tonnes.
"We are at too high levels," Nordin said.
